skill.name: Spot the bias: what is left out or made one-sided
skill.why: A one-sided text can fool you without telling a single lie.
skill.how: Ask what's missing, who the text favours, and how the other side would tell it.

steps.say: Maxx posted: 'I saved a lizard!' Here's what the ranger saw.

steps.win: Right! The hat doesn't matter. The mum does. Hiding what matters makes a text one-sided, or biased.

creature.name: Flipscale
creature.blurb: A shingleback lizard whose stumpy tail looks just like its head, so there is always another end to check. It sniffs out stories that only show you one side.

encounters.text: MAXX'S CAPTION: 'Found this little quoll shivering on a rock at dawn, poor thing. The beach is sparkling now. That's what heroes do. Stay gold!' VOLUNTEERS' REPORT: On Saturday, Bluster Beach was cleaned from end to end. Sixty volunteers worked for six hours and filled 85 bags. The rubbish included bottles, old fishing nets and a single thong. Maxx Vantablack picked up one plastic bottle on camera. By the end of the day, the beach was clean. Maxx stayed for about ten minutes, then left on his jet ski. The volunteers say they will be back next month, with or without cameras. The bags were collected by the council truck on Monday morning. The volunteers found the most rubbish near the boat ramp, where the wind blows it into the rocks. Next month's clean-up starts at 8 am at the surf club, and gloves will be provided. Everyone is welcome.

encounters.frame: The Bluster Rock council has voted on a new skate park. Two very different reports landed on the deck of the Soggy Biscuit.
encounters.text: THE BLUSTER BUGLE: SKATE PARK PUSHED THROUGH. Despite strong concerns from residents, the council voted 5 to 2 on Tuesday night to build a $180,000 skate park beside the oval. Shop owner Doug Harris told the meeting that the noise would drive customers away from the main street. 'It's a waste of money,' said long-time resident Jean Albury. 'Nobody asked the people who actually live here.' Construction will begin in January, and the park is expected to open in March. THE BLUSTER SKATE CLUB NEWSLETTER: More than 200 people packed the hall for Tuesday's council meeting, the biggest crowd in years. Thirty-four people spoke: 26 in favour of the skate park and 8 against. Year 6 students presented a petition with 600 signatures and a model of the design that they had built in class. Councillors heard that a state sports grant would pay half of the $180,000 cost, so the island would pay $90,000. Two shop owners said they were worried about noise, and the council agreed to plant a row of trees between the park and the main street. The council then voted 5 to 2 in favour. Building starts in January.
encounters.prompt: How is the Bugle's report biased?
encounters.success: The Bugle quotes just two people against the park. It skips the 26 speakers for it, the petition and grant.

options.text: It quotes only people against the park, although most speakers supported it.
Its only problem is the tilted headline 'pushed through'. Nothing important is missing.
options.reason: That headline does tilt it, but the Bugle also hides the 26 speakers for the park.

options.text: It leaves out the vote count, so readers can't tell who won.
options.reason: The Bugle does give the count, 5 to 2, in its first sentence.

options.text: It gives the opening date, which tilts readers towards the park.
options.reason: An opening date is a plain fact. It doesn't make readers feel for or against the park.

encounters.text: PET SHOP LEAFLET: Shinglebacks make the perfect family pet! These gentle, slow-moving lizards are calm enough to sit on your lap, and they rarely bite. They eat a simple diet of fruit, snails and a little tinned dog food, so feeding them is easy and cheap. Their stumpy tails and bright blue tongues make them a favourite with kids. Pick up a Shingleback Starter Kit, including a glass tank, a heat lamp and a water bowl, for just $199 at Scales and Tails. RANGER STATION CARE GUIDE: Shinglebacks are native lizards found across southern and western Australia, including the dry country around Bluster Rock. Most shinglebacks are calm, and they will usually sit quietly if they are handled gently. They eat snails and fruit, and in captivity they can also be given a little meat, such as dog food. Shinglebacks can live for more than fifty years, so a pet bought for a child may outlive its owner's childhood by decades. They need a warm tank with a heat lamp and a bowl of fresh water. Anyone keeping a shingleback on the island must hold a reptile keeper's licence from the ranger station.

encounters.frame: A rocket was launched from the far end of Bluster Rock. Zed wrote a note comparing the company's report with the Bugle's.
encounters.text: SKYWARD ROCKET COMPANY, NEWS RELEASE: Today, our Skyward 4 rocket lifted off from the Bluster Rock launch pad at 6:02 am in perfect weather. Just nine minutes later, it placed a new weather satellite into orbit around the Earth, exactly on schedule. The satellite will help farmers across the region plan for rain and drought. We thank our team of 300 engineers for a successful launch, and we look forward to our next mission in June. THE BLUSTER BUGLE: Skyward 4 launched from the island at 6:02 this morning and successfully carried a weather satellite into orbit. However, the rocket's reusable booster, which was meant to land upright on a barge, missed the barge and crashed into the sea about 40 kilometres off the coast. Pieces of the booster have since washed up on two beaches. The harbour master has closed the fishing grounds for a week while divers search for fuel tanks, and local fishers say they will lose a week's income. When asked about the booster, a Skyward spokesperson said the company 'does not comment on test equipment'.

encounters.frame: Indi read a glowing review of the Red Rock Music Festival. Then she found the letters page in the same week's Bugle.
encounters.text: FESTIVAL REVIEW: The Red Rock Music Festival returned to Bluster Rock last weekend, and what a weekend it was. Over three days, 22 bands played on two stages beneath the glowing face of the rock. The crowd of about 4,000 danced well past midnight on both Friday and Saturday. Headliners The Salt Pans closed the festival with a ninety-minute set that had the whole crowd singing along. 'Best weekend of my life,' said one fan, wearing a hat made of glow sticks. The food trucks sold out of dumplings by Saturday afternoon. LETTERS TO THE EDITOR, SAME WEEK: 'The music could be heard twelve kilometres away until 2 am on both nights. My baby didn't sleep at all,' wrote Lena Baxter of Gum Flat. 'The car park overflowed, and festival-goers parked across my driveway,' wrote Ray Kidd. 'On Monday morning, I counted more than 300 cans and bottles along the creek near the camping ground,' wrote Ranger Dot. 'The festival raised $8,000 for the new school library,' wrote Mia Tran, who lives beside the oval. The festival organisers say they are planning to hold the event again next year, and will meet with residents in February.

encounters.frame: Two newspapers ran headlines about the Reef Rays' coach. Tully has read the full story, and she's fuming about one of them.
encounters.text: THE FULL STORY: Reef Rays coach Ana Ferris announced on Monday that she will step down at the end of the season. Ferris has coached the Rays for eight seasons and led them to two premierships, in 2019 and 2022. The team has lost its last five matches, its worst run since she took over. At a press conference, Ferris said the decision was her own. 'I've given this club everything for eight years,' she said. 'It's time for someone with fresh ideas, and it's time for me to spend some weekends with my family.' Club president Hamid Rauf said the board had asked her to stay for another two years, but respected her choice. Players said they wanted to win the last three matches of the season for her. Ferris began as a player with the Rays in 2005 and played 112 games before becoming coach. Under her, the club also started its first junior girls' team, which now has more than 80 players. The board will announce a new coach before next season. HEADLINE A, THE ISLAND BUZZ: RAYS COACH QUITS AFTER SHOCK LOSING STREAK. HEADLINE B, THE BLUSTER BUGLE: RAYS COACH RESIGNS AFTER FIVE STRAIGHT LOSSES, ENDING EIGHT SEASONS AND TWO PREMIERSHIPS.
encounters.prompt: Which statement about the headlines is best supported by the full story?
encounters.success: Headline A keeps the bad news and drops the premierships. 'Quits' and 'shock' tilt it further against Ferris.

options.text: Headline B is biased, because it mentions the five losses.
options.reason: The losses are true, and B balances them with her two premierships.

options.text: Headline A is biased: it leaves out her premierships and uses tilted words like 'quits'.
Headline A is biased, because it is shorter than Headline B.
options.reason: Length isn't bias. A short headline can be fair if it doesn't tilt or hide things.

options.text: Neither headline is biased, because both of them mention the losing streak and the coach's decision to go.
options.reason: Both mention the losses, but only B adds the premierships. A leaves out her successes.

encounters.frame: Maxx is selling a new robot at Vantamart. Gus hacked into the Vantamart customer complaints log. (He says it's not hacking. It's science.)
encounters.text: THE VANTAMART AD: 'Meet MaxxBot, the robot that's as awesome as me! MaxxBot can dance, take selfies and say forty of my famous catchphrases, including "Stay gold!" It's covered in real gold-coloured paint and stands 50 centimetres tall. Over 10,000 MaxxBots have been sold this month. Get yours for just $349, only at Vantamart!' THE VANTAMART COMPLAINTS LOG, THIS MONTH: 1,840 complaints received. Most common complaint: the battery lasts about twenty minutes, then takes six hours to charge. Second most common: the gold paint flakes off and sticks to carpets and pets. Third most common: MaxxBot shouts 'Smash that heart button!' at full volume at random times, including in the middle of the night. Customers report that it does dance, take selfies and say its catchphrases. On the 14th, Vantamart quietly stopped selling MaxxBot in two countries after reports that its wheels could trap small fingers. Each MaxxBot comes in a gold box with a poster of Maxx, a charging cable and a booklet of dance moves. The log also lists 212 customers who have asked for a refund, and 9 who asked if it could be switched off for good. A note at the bottom of the log, in gold pen, says: 'Do NOT put any of this in the ads.'
